o.text: From Proto-Common Turkic *yinčü, ultimately from Middle Chinese 珍珠 (MC trin tsyu) ~ 眞珠 (MC tsyin tsyu).

Borrowed from Russian босяк (bosjak). Judging from folk etymologies, influenced by Azerbaijani pas (“rust”) as to refer to rusty, impure senses and reanalyzed under similarity of Azerbaijani passiv (“passive”). Originated in military slang.
Partial calque of Persian باز آمدن (bâz âmadan). Cognate with Turkish vazgeçmek.
